paper_title: Searching for solar axions using data from the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory
notes: Solar axion search via deuteron axiodissociation (a+d->n+p) at SNO. Primary constraint is on isovector axion-nucleon coupling |g3_aN|=(1/2)|gan-gap| > 2e-5 GeV^-1 (in derivative-coupling units, GeV^-1) at 95% CL for axion masses up to ~5.5 MeV, with a solar-trapping upper bound near 1e-3 GeV^-1. The paper recasts this as a limit on gan assuming no cancellation between gan and gap, hence AxionNeutron chosen per hint, but note the natural quantity is g3_aN (could also be AxionProton). Coupling has units GeV^-1 (derivative coupling), not dimensionless. Data points trace the lower edge of the excluded band; mass range covers sub-MeV to ~5.5 MeV. Not a DM haloscope (solar flux), so no DM density assumed. | Auto-corrected masses: Hz→eV (×4.136e-15, rule=argmin|log10(median*f)-log10(anchor=1.0e-08)|)
